description: The same loud, well-attended candle, with a healthy book for the week before it and a near-empty book stamped on its own day. The day's snapshot was read after the candle closed, so it is not evidence; the check completes on the week before and passes.
labelling_rationale: SLS v1.0.20 §6.4, 'The depth input': 'A snapshot taken after the candle's close is never read (no look-ahead).' **The candle** is s7-a-thin-book-makes-an-abnormal-candle-suspect's: 2026-08-21T00:00, RVOL 5.0 (ABNORMAL), 30 trades against a median of 10 (participants pass), closing at 2026-08-21T04:00. **The snapshots.** Seven at 100, stamped 2026-08-14 .. 2026-08-20, and one at 1 stamped 2026-08-21. The stamp is the start of the UTC day; the book behind it is read when the daily job runs, later that day, so the 2026-08-21 book may well have been read after 04:00. The owner's ruling (Bundle D M2 Q1) treats a snapshot stamped day D as taken at the end of day D: only a candle closing at or after 2026-08-22T00:00 may read the 2026-08-21 one. **The verdict.** This candle reads the 2026-08-20 snapshot (100) against the median of 2026-08-14 .. 2026-08-20 (100). 100 >= 50, so the depth test passes, both tests ran, and the candle is validated and not suspect. Nothing is recorded: §6.4 records only a suspect. Had the engine read the 2026-08-21 stamp, the depth would be 1 and the candle would be tagged -- on a book from after its close.
